title: Vass family fears justice will not be served
subtitle: Four officers charged: Otto Vass died after scuffle with police in August: [Toronto Edition]
article: The four police officers charged with manslaughter in the death of _Otto_ _Vass_ will go free unless the Attorney-General's office gives the prosecution the proper resources to make the case, a lawyer for the _Vass_ family says.
Mr. _Vass_, 55, a father of five, died on Aug. 9 after a scuffle with police in the parking lot of the 7-Eleven store at Lansdowne Avenue and College Street.
Julian Falconer said trials involving Toronto police officers are tough to win because their union spends millions of dollars to defend them.
"We've had inexperienced Crown attorneys who have been operating with less than adequate resources, fighting veritable dream teams," he said.
Mr. Falconer said the Attorney- General has taken a small step to ensure a balanced trial by assigning Desmond McGarry, a senior Crown prosecutor, to this case.

Yesterday, after an 11-week investigation by the province's Special Investigations Unit, four officers from 14 Division -- Constables Robert LeMaitre, Phillip Duncan, Nam-Nhat Le and Filippo Bevilacqua -- were charged with manslaughter.
The SIU investigates circumstances involving police and civilians that result in serious injury, sexual assault or death.
About 100 witnesses, including civilians, police officers and emergency services personnel, were interviewed by 16 investigators, said Peter A. Tinsley, director of the SIU.
The investigators uncovered evidence, including a surveillance video seized from inside the 7- Eleven, that shows reasonable grounds to believe that the four officers are criminally liable, he said.

"What is inherent in causing these charges to be laid is the belief that the actions of the officers contributed substantially or significantly to the ultimate death," said Mr. Tinsley. "The acts of the police officers were unlawful and not legally justified."
Craig Bromell, president of the Toronto Police Association, condemned the charges laid against the officers.
"We're very upset and angry," said Mr. Bromell. "We completely support them and we're going to make sure they get through this."
The officers were performing their duties the way they were trained, Mr. Bromell said.
"When you get into a violent situation, a lot of times for survival reasons, you have to do everything you can to survive. The officers did that to make sure they went home that night," he said.
Chief Julian Fantino also expressed dismay that the officers were charged.

"Any loss of life is tragic for all involved, including the police officers. I am disappointed that these charges have been laid against four of my officers, but we must now let due process take its course," he said in a written statement.
"He shouldn't be expressing an opinion whatsoever," Mr. Falconer said. "What he's saying is they ought not to have been charged. That's the message he's sending, clearly."

At the time of the incident, reports said that Mr. _Vass_ had a history of mental illness and had become aggressive when the officers asked for identification. It was also reported that Mr. _Vass_ took numerous blows to the head and arms, consistent with the use of nightsticks.

The four officers turned themselves in at the SIU offices in Mississauga yesterday. They were released on conditions, including surrendering their firearms. They have all been reassigned to desk duties.
